chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Muhammad al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the Words of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'They ask you about the spoils of war.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who dies and has no guardian (mawla), then his wealth is from the spoils of war (anfal).'

key_terms.الْأَنْفَالِ: Spoils of war; specifically refers to public treasury or state assets in this legal context
key_terms.مَوْلًى: Guardian or heir; refers to a person with legal authority over the deceased's affairs

ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of a deceased person who has no heirs or guardian according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the application of Surah Al-Anfal, linking the term 'al-Anfal' specifically to the estate of a deceased person who lacks a 'mawla' (a guardian or inheritor to claim the property). In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes the mechanism for 'Gharib' (stranger/dead ender) inheritance, where the estate reverts to the Imam or the public treasury, reflecting the Quranic principle that ultimate ownership and distribution of surplus wealth belong to God and His Messenger.
